To find stationary points, take the first derivative f'(x), set it equal to zero, and solve for x. Then, plug those x-values back into f(x) to get y-coordinates. For example, if f(x) = x³ - 3x, f'(x) = 3x² - 3. Setting to zero gives x = ±1, so stationary points are (1, -2) and (-1, 2).
